recipes.title: Aloo Bonda
recipes.description: Spiced potato balls dipped in gram flour batter and deep fried until golden, a South Indian teatime snack.

steps.instructionText: Boil the potatoes, peel them and mash coarsely.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a pan. When hot, add the green chillies and fry for a few seconds.
Add the onion and fry until browned.
Add the ginger and garlic and fry for 1 minute.
Fold in the coriander leaves, mashed potatoes and salt. Let cool, then shape into golf-ball-sized balls.
For the batter, mix the besan, rice flour, baking soda and salt.
Add enough water to make a smooth batter, slightly thicker than ketchup.
Heat oil for deep frying, at least 4 cm deep, in a deep pan.
Dip each potato ball in the batter so it is completely coated, and slide it into the hot oil. Don't overcrowd the pan.
Fry the bondas until golden, then drain. Serve hot with chutney or ketchup.

recipes.title: Kadhi Pakora
recipes.description: Tangy buttermilk and besan curry tempered with mustard and curry leaves, with fried besan pakoras soaked in.

steps.instructionText: For the pakoras, mix the 1 cup besan with water, salt and turmeric powder to make a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a large pan for frying.
Drop round spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil so the pakoras come out round and fluffy.
Fry the pakoras until golden, then lift them out of the oil.
For the curry, whisk the buttermilk with the 1 tbsp gram flour, turmeric powder, hing and salt until smooth and lump-free.
Heat a little oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds, garlic, ginger, curry leaves and onion, and fry until slightly reddish.
Stir the buttermilk mixture and pour it into the pan. Keep stirring over medium heat until it starts bubbling.
Add the pakoras and lower the heat. Leave them in the kadhi for a while, then cover and switch off the heat.
Serve hot with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Chapati (Roti)
recipes.description: Soft whole wheat flatbread cooked on a hot dry tava, the everyday bread of North India.

steps.instructionText: Mix the whole wheat flour and salt. Add the warm water a little at a time, kneading until the dough is smooth but not too sticky.
Cover the dough and let it rest for at least 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls. Roll each into a thin disc, sprinkling with flour as you roll.
Heat an ungreased tava or pan over moderately high heat until very hot.
Put a chapati on the hot pan and press it with a spatula or a dry cloth so it puffs up.
Flip it and cook until lightly browned on both sides.
Brush with ghee if you like, and serve warm.

recipes.title: Chicken Vindaloo
recipes.description: Hot, tangy Goan-style chicken curry in a vinegar-browned onion sauce with garlic, chilli and black pepper.

steps.instructionText: Heat enough oil to cover the base of a heavy frying pan. Slice the onions into thin slivers and add them to the very hot oil.
Turn the heat to low and let the onions sauté gently for about 3 minutes, until they start to caramelize.
Gradually raise the heat and keep stirring until the onions brown heavily without burning.
Add the white wine vinegar and stir until it evaporates. Keep frying until the onions are very brown but not burnt.
Lift out the onions, letting the oil drip back. Blend them with 1 tbsp oil for about 1 minute into a thick, dark brown sauce.
Chop the garlic, ginger and deseeded chillies and blend to a grainy paste. Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala and cinnamon powder.
Crush the black peppercorns coarsely, then grind in the mustard seeds and rock salt. Stir this powder into the paste.
Heat a little oil in a saucepan and add the spice paste. When it bubbles, add the chicken and stir until browned and mostly cooked.
Add the onion sauce and stir for 1 minute.
Add the water and stir for 2 minutes, then turn the heat to low. The sauce should be quite runny at this stage.
Cover and cook for 30-40 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes so it doesn't stick. The sauce will darken.
Spoon the vindaloo over boiled basmati rice and sprinkle with the coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Coconut Chutney
recipes.description: Fresh coconut ground with roasted chana dal, green chillies and ginger, finished with a mustard tempering.

steps.instructionText: Dry roast the chana dal until browned, then let it cool.
Grind the roasted chana dal, coconut, green chillies, tamarind paste, coriander leaves, ginger paste and salt with as little water as possible.
The chutney should be somewhere between a coarse and a smooth paste.
For the tempering, heat the oil in a small ladle and add the mustard seeds. Let them crackle.
As the crackling dies down, add the hing and curry leaves and stir for a few seconds.
Pour the tempering over the chutney and mix well.

recipes.title: Dabeli
recipes.description: Kutchi street snack of toasted pav stuffed with spiced potato, sweet and garlic chutneys, sev and peanuts.

ingredients.name: roasted peanuts, plus extra to garnish

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a pan. Add the hing, dabeli masala, mashed potatoes, salt and a sprinkle of water. Mix very well so the masala coats the potatoes.
Mix in the green chillies, if using.
Take off the heat and taste. Add a little more dabeli masala if you want it spicier, then toss in 2 tbsp of the roasted peanuts and mix well.
Slice each pav in half and toast the halves with a little butter on a griddle.
Spread garlic chutney on one cut side and tamarind date chutney on the other.
Place a portion of the potato filling between the halves.
Top the filling with chopped onion, coriander leaves and sev.
Press the pav down, garnish with the pomegranate seeds and more peanuts, and serve right away with extra chutney.

recipes.title: Onion Pakoda
recipes.description: Crunchy Tamil Nadu-style fritters of onion and peanuts in a spiced, crumbly gram flour dough.

steps.instructionText: Mix the besan, rice flour, green gram flour, hing, turmeric, cayenne pepper, curry leaves, cumin powder and crushed black peppercorns.
Add the onion, peanuts, 1 tsp oil and salt. Mix well and set aside for about 10 minutes so the onion releases its moisture.
Add the water a little at a time to make a crumbly dough that holds in chunks but breaks with light pressure. Too much water makes them soft.
Heat the oil for deep frying in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Pinch off chunks of the dough and deep fry them in medium-hot oil until golden brown and crisp.
Serve the pakoda hot or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Mirchi Bada
recipes.description: Large green chillies stuffed with spiced mashed potato, coated in besan batter and deep fried.

steps.instructionText: Slit the large green chillies lengthwise, remove the seeds and set aside.
Boil the potatoes in salted water, then peel and mash them well.
Mix the red chilli powder, chaat masala and coriander leaves into the potatoes.
Make a thick batter with the besan, water, turmeric powder and salt.
Fill the chillies with the potato mixture, then dip them in the batter so they are completely covered.
Deep fry the battered chillies in hot oil until golden brown.

recipes.title: Punugulu
recipes.description: Crisp fritters of fermented urad dal and rice rava batter, studded with onion and green chilli.

steps.instructionText: Soak the urad dal in water for several hours.
Soak the rice rava in water in a separate bowl.
Grind the soaked urad dal to a slightly loose batter, then mix in the soaked rice rava.
Mix in the maida, adding a little water to thin the batter if needed.
Stir in the onions, green chillies and salt. Leave the batter to ferment and rise.
Heat the oil for deep frying. Drop in small balls of batter and fry until golden.

recipes.title: White Dhokla (Rice & Urad Dal)
recipes.description: Soft, tangy Gujarati steamed cake of fermented rice and urad dal batter, topped with coriander.

steps.instructionText: Toast the rice and urad dal in a pan over medium heat for 4-5 minutes.
Let cool, then grind to a semi-coarse powder and tip it into a bowl.
Whisk in the yogurt and warm water until there are no lumps and the batter is of pouring consistency.
Add salt and leave the batter to ferment for 8-10 hours.
Grind the ginger and green chillies to a paste and mix it into the fermented batter.
Grease a dhokla plate or thali with a little oil, and bring water to a boil in the steamer.
Set half the batter aside. Mix 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp oil and 1/2 tbsp lemon juice into the other half.
Pour it into the greased plate and steam for 8-10 minutes, until a knife poked in comes out clean.
Repeat with the remaining batter, baking soda, oil and lemon juice, mixing them in just before steaming.
Sprinkle with the coriander leaves and serve hot with green chutney.

recipes.title: Ghevar
recipes.description: Rajasthani honeycomb disc of ghee and flour batter, fried in a ring mould and dipped in sugar syrup.

steps.instructionText: Simmer the sugar and 1/2 cup water to a one-string syrup. Take off the heat and keep warm.
Combine the maida, arrowroot, melted ghee and kewra essence in a bowl.
For the batter, whisk in 1 cup of the water in a very thin stream, so the ghee and water form an emulsion and don't separate.
Whisk in the other 2 cups water the same way, to a very thin batter, thinner than crepe batter. Keep it in a cool place.
Heat ghee for deep frying in a kadhai with a ghevar mould or metal ring set in it. The ghee should come 3/4 of the way up the mould.
Over medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter in a thin stream into the centre of the mould. It will froth and spread to the edges.
When the froth subsides, pour in another spoonful. Use a skewer to keep a hole in the centre. Repeat about seven times.
Raise the heat and pour a few ladlefuls of hot ghee into the centre to cook it through.
When the centre is firm and the ghevar is golden, lift it out with a skewer through the centre and let the excess ghee drip off.
Dip the ghevar in the sugar syrup, drain quickly and place on a serving plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make 10 ghevar in all.

recipes.title: Gulab Jamun
recipes.description: Soft milk-powder dumplings fried dark brown and soaked overnight in cardamom sugar syrup.

steps.instructionText: Heat oil 4-5 cm deep in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Mix the milk powder, baking mix and melted butter in a bowl.
Add the warm milk 2 tbsp at a time, mixing with a wooden spoon, until you have a firm, moist dough that is not sticky.
Roll into evenly sized balls and fry them within a few minutes, before they dry out.
Fry a few balls at a time without crowding the pan, stirring so they brown evenly. They sink at first, then float.
When dark brown, lift them out and drain on paper. Repeat with the rest of the dough.
Take the seeds out of the cardamom pods and crush them lightly.
Heat the water, sugar and cardamom for 10 minutes. Don't overheat, or the syrup will caramelize.
Soak the gulab jamuns in the syrup overnight. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Homemade Paneer
recipes.description: Fresh Indian cheese made by curdling boiling milk with lemon juice, then draining and pressing it.

steps.instructionText: Bring the milk to a boil in a large pan.
Just before it boils, add the lemon juice to curdle the milk.
Pour the curdled milk through a cheesecloth to drain off most of the whey.
Press out the water firmly, then put a weight on top of the paneer.
Leave it in the fridge for 2-3 hours to rest and firm up.

recipes.title: Double ka Meetha
recipes.description: Hyderabadi bread pudding: ghee-fried bread soaked in cardamom milk syrup with khoa, nuts and raisins.

steps.instructionText: Trim the crusts off the bread slices and cut each slice into four.
Fry the bread pieces in the ghee until golden brown.
Dissolve the sugar in the water to make a syrup. Add the milk and boil until it starts to thicken.
Grind the cardamom seeds to a powder.
Stir the cardamom powder and khoa into the thickened milk.
Arrange the fried bread on a flat tray and pour the syrup over it while the bread is still hot.
Garnish with the raisins, almonds, cashews and pistachios. Chill and serve.

recipes.title: Idli
recipes.description: Soft, fluffy steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal batter, the classic South Indian breakfast.

steps.instructionText: Wash the idli rice and urad dal thoroughly.
Soak the rice in one bowl, and the urad dal with the methi in another, for no more than 2 hours. Use about twice as much water as dal.
Drain both. Keep the dal soaking water, but discard the rice soaking water.
Grind the urad dal to a fine paste, adding a little of its soaking water if needed.
Grind the rice to a coarse paste with about 1 cup of the filtered water, or less if you can.
Mix the rice and urad dal pastes together well and season with the salt.
Set the batter aside somewhere warm to ferment for 8 hours.
Grease the idli moulds well with oil.
Gently spoon in the batter without stirring, so the trapped bubbles stay in for a fluffy texture.
Steam for 12 minutes.
Ease the idlis out of the moulds with a thin knife or spatula. Serve hot with sambar.

recipes.title: Bhapa Doi with Spiced Figs
recipes.description: Baked sweet yoghurt with cardamom, pistachios and raisins, topped with figs poached in spiced lemon syrup.

steps.instructionText: Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Preheat the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan). Line four ramekins with paper muffin cases.
Whisk the condensed milk, yoghurt and cardamom powder together, then fold in the pistachios and raisins.
Pour into the ramekins and stand them in a roasting tin. Pour warm water into the tin to come almost halfway up their sides.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, until set.
Meanwhile, pare the zest from the lemon and squeeze out 1 tsp of juice.
Heat the sugar, water, lemon zest and juice, cloves, cinnamon and star anise over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a boil.
Cut each fig into four, add to the syrup and simmer for 2 minutes. Take off the heat and let the figs cool in the syrup.
Lift the ramekins out of the water bath and let them cool.
Unmould the puddings onto plates, arrange the figs on top and drizzle the syrup around.

recipes.title: Chhundo (Sweet Mango Pickle)
recipes.description: Gujarati sweet and spicy grated raw mango pickle with cumin and chilli, cooked slowly in the sun for days.

steps.instructionText: Peel the mangoes and grate them finely.
Mix the grated mangoes evenly with the sugar, salt, red chilli powder, cumin powder and turmeric powder.
Spread the mixture in a shallow, wide-mouthed jar and cover it with a thin cloth.
Keep the jar in the sun for 5 days, stirring three times a day, until the syrup reaches one-string consistency.

recipes.title: Moong Dal
recipes.description: Simple pressure-cooked moong dal with green chillies and turmeric, finished with a cumin and curry leaf tadka.

steps.instructionText: Put the moong dal, green chillies, turmeric powder and water in a pressure cooker. Cook for 15 minutes, then let the pressure release on its own.
Open the cooker and mash the dal. Add salt, and a little more water if it is too thick, and heat through over medium heat.
Heat the oil or ghee in a small pan and add the jeera and curry leaves.
When they splutter, pour the tadka over the dal. Serve hot with rice or rotis.

recipes.title: Jalebi
recipes.description: Crisp loops of fermented flour batter, deep fried and dunked in rose-scented sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: oil or ghee, for deep frying

steps.instructionText: Mix the maida, besan, baking powder and 1 1/2 cups water into a smooth batter.
Leave the batter uncovered at room temperature overnight, about 12 hours.
For the syrup, stir the sugar, 3 cups water and cream of tartar over moderate heat until the sugar dissolves.
Turn the heat to high and boil for 5 minutes.
Let the syrup cool, stir in the rose water and tint it light orange with the food colouring.
Heat the oil or ghee in a wide kadhai to about 175 °C (350 °F).
Spoon the batter into a piping bag with a 5 mm opening. If it is too thick to squeeze, mix in a little water.
Pipe the batter into the hot oil in loops and figure-eights on top of each other, about 7 cm across.
Fry each jalebi until golden brown, drain off the oil, and soak it in the syrup for 1 minute before serving.

recipes.title: Jigarthanda
recipes.description: Madurai's chilled milk drink with almond gum jelly, nannari syrup, caramel milk, ice cream and malai.

steps.instructionText: Wash the badam pisin and soak it in the 250 ml water overnight, until it swells into a jelly. Keep it in the fridge.
For the syrup, wash and crush the nannari root. Bring the 300 ml water to a boil, add the root and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the 150 g sugar and cook to a one-string syrup. Cool and store airtight.
For the ice cream, boil 1 1/2 l of the milk, stirring until frothy, and collect the malai that forms.
Whip the fresh cream and stir it into the milk. Lower the heat, stir in 4 tbsp of the sugar until dissolved, then mix in the khova.
Melt 2 tbsp of the sugar in a heavy pan over low heat until it caramelizes. Carefully pour in the hot milk mixture and stir until smooth.
Let cool, pour into an airtight container, cover with cling film and freeze for 4-5 hours.
Beat the set ice cream with a whisk or blender, 3-4 times for creaminess, then freeze again for 5-6 hours.
For the drink, simmer the remaining 1 l milk until reduced by half, collecting the malai that forms.
Caramelize the last 4 tbsp sugar in another pan, stir it into the milk until golden, and simmer for 10 minutes. Cool and chill.
Put 1-2 tbsp of the almond gum jelly and 1 tbsp nannari syrup in a tall glass. Fill it 3/4 full with the jigarthanda milk.
Add a scoop of the ice cream, top with the collected malai and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Kacchi Chicken Biryani
recipes.description: Raw chicken marinated in yoghurt, fried onions and mint, layered with part-cooked rice and slow-cooked on dum.

ingredients.name: large onions, sliced and fried in ghee
whole spices (black cardamom, kala jeera, pepper, cinnamon)

steps.instructionText: Mix most of the fried onions with the yoghurt, chopped green chillies, mint leaves, ghee, 1 tsp garam masala, salt and ginger-garlic paste.
Add the chicken and leave to marinate for at least 4-5 hours.
Bring a pot of water to a boil with the whole spices, salt and oil, then add the rice.
Cook the rice until almost tender but not fully cooked, then drain.
Spread a very thin layer of rice in a heavy pot. Add the marinated chicken, then cover it with the rest of the rice.
Mix the saffron into a little milk. Put a piece of butter in each quarter of the pot and pour the lemon juice and saffron milk over the rice.
Push the whole green chillies into the rice. Scatter over the coriander leaves, the remaining fried onions and a sprinkle of garam masala.
Seal the pot tightly with foil so no steam escapes. Cook over high heat for about 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 30-35 minutes more, turning the pot every 10 minutes for even heating.
Check that the chicken and rice are fully cooked, then serve.

recipes.title: Khandvi (Gram Flour Rolls)
recipes.description: Silky Gujarati rolls of besan cooked in spiced buttermilk, spread thin, rolled and topped with seeds.

ingredients.name: jalapeño or other green chilli, finely diced

steps.instructionText: Whisk the besan, buttermilk, ground ginger, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt into a smooth batter with no lumps.
Heat 2-3 tsp oil in a kadhai or pan over medium-low heat and pour in the batter.
Stir continuously so no lumps form, until the mixture thickens almost to a dough.
To test, spread a little on a greased surface, let it cool and try to roll it up. If it won't roll, cook it a little longer.
When ready, quickly spread the mixture very thinly, thinner than a crepe, on a greased sheet. Let it cool.
Cut the cooled sheet into strips and roll each strip up.
Garnish with the mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, jalapeño and coconut.
